newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends weaker on rate speculation.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends weaker on rate speculation.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended weaker on Thursday at C$1.3764 (US$0.7265) from Wednesday's close of C$1.3731 (US$0.7282) under pressure from speculation the Bank of Canada could be pushed to raise short-term interest rates, dealers said. * They said the currency was expected to weaken further overnight as overseas players join the call for a rate rise.
The Canadian dollar eased after Statistics Canada reported that the nation's consumer price index was slightly higher than expected in June.

Statistics Canada reported the unadjusted consumer price index (CPI) for June rose 0.2 percent in the month. A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the seasonally unadjusted CPI to rise 0.1 percent on the month.

"Some people are reading the inflation numbers as possibly triggering a Bank tightening, and they bought a little bit of Canada (dollars)," said Stephen Wateridge, managing director of corporate foreign exchange at CIBC Wood Gundy.
Economists said hard-driving speculators will try to push the currency to levels where the Bank of Canada may have to act to defend the currency.

"The market is now going to try test the bank by pushing the currency higher to see if they can prompt a rate hike," said Andrew Pyle, head of fixed income research with ABN AMRO Bank Canada, noting that a move beyond C$1.3830 (US$0.7230) could prompt the Bank of Canada to hike rates.
Hall said upcoming economic numbers may increase the pressure on the Bank of Canada to raise rates as merchandise trade and wholesale trade numbers come out.
"Forthcoming numbers will set the stage, but I don't think the Bank of Canada recognizes the script," Hall said.
A Reuter survey of economists forecast a merchandise trade surplus of C$2.22 billion for May and that wholesale trade will rise by one percent in May
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar fell against the German mark to 1.2999 marks from 1.3033 marks at Wednesday's close, and held steady at 84.05 yen.
